answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock 100 credits for a 30-day horizon before it may bid on jobs. The bond stays frozen while the identity trades, so recycling the same credits cannot activate more accounts. Each extra fake identity costs an attacker another 100 credits in tied-up capital, plus the interest or trading returns forgone during the lock. Names like nectar or fable are free; simultaneous access is scarce because every account needs its own bond.
